articles.title: WSL roundup: Chelsea thwarted by Liverpool keeper, London City move to third
articles.summary: Keating’s resilience keeps Chelsea at bay in 0-0 draw. Van de Donk and Putellas score twice to sink Palace 6-2. Khiara Keating’s resilient performance in goal denied Chelsea, the Women’s Super League leaders, and earned Liverpool a point, while London City Lionesses moved to within four points of…
body: After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night, Chelsea drew a blank. Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after beating City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the form of Aggie Beever-Jones, who scored her first WSL goal in more than a year in the 6-0 defeat of Charlton, have left Chelsea’s attack short.

Despite almost 70% possession and 47 touches in the box to Liverpool’s 12, Sonia Bompastor’s side amassed only 19 shots to Liverpool’s 13 and seven on target to their opponents’ four. Although the Blues remain unbeaten in the WSL, their third draw in five games in all competitions means City can leapfrog them at the top if they beat Tottenham on Sunday.
Liverpool had chances, particularly in the first half, but were hanging on after the break and Keating helped them to a fourth clean sheet, a tally bettered only by Bompastor’s side.

articles.title: European football: Doué carried off for PSG while Kane vows to return fresh
articles.summary: Doué injury adds to that of Kvaratskhelia last month. Nice 2-3 PSG; Lazio 3-0 Lecce; Gladbach 0-1 Dortmund. Désiré Doué was carried off in tears after suffering what looked like a nasty knee injury as Paris Saint-Germain beat Nice 3-2 in Ligue 1.
body: Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. He looked to be in agony as he clutched his right knee, and the match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment before being carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium.

PSG will now be dreading discovering the extent of the injury, having lost Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee playing against Barcelona last month. The Georgian winger is unlikely to return this season, and Doué looks set for a significant spell on the sidelines too.
“We will need to wait until tomorrow for the test results, but it is obviously a serious injury,” PSG’s coach, Luis Enrique, told the broadcaster Ligue 1+.
Mohamed Amoura had given Nice the lead only for Senny Mayulu to equalise with a penalty awarded after a video assistant referee check for a handball.

articles.title: Ireland remind themselves that the best are beatable
articles.summary: Ireland put a string of deflating losses against the world's best teams behind them with a hard-fought 20-17 win over South Africa in Dublin.
body: After six deflating losses in a row to South Africa, New Zealand and France, Andy Farrell was asked this week what made him think Ireland could get back to the levels they had reached when considered squarely among that group.
Because they had got there before came the typically uncomplicated response from the side's head coach.

The longer the 2023 World Cup receded into memory, however, fewer and fewer believed that his side still had within them the type of performance they produced to beat the Springboks 20-17 on Saturday.

Undoubtedly Ireland's biggest win of recent years, having not beaten one of the three sides who started this weekend above them in the rankings since the summer of 2024, this was one of their most needed too.

articles.summary: Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan on target. Hearts thrash Dundee 8-0; Frick makes winning start. The recalled midfielders Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan both scored as Celtic beat St Mirren 4-1.
body: The centre-forward Camilo Duran was also on target as Celtic killed the game late in the first half with three goals in nine minutes. Callum McGregor grabbed his first league goal of the season before Killian Phillips scored a consolation from the spot.
With Baur facing up to 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Nygren nursing a heel problem, Martin O’Neill would have been delighted with how his midfield functioned.

Oxlade-Chamberlain made his fifth start of the season and McCowan his second. The pair had never started a game together before. O’Neill also introduced the former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joël van den Berg for a debut in the second half and the 19-year-old showed some good touches.
Celtic started with a new-look front three of Duran flanked by Jota and Yang Hyun-jun. Duran was a constant threat and had two goals disallowed for offside in the opening quarter.

articles.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge. Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table.
body: Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager.

With hindsight, Michael Carrick’s dismissal was probably inevitable from the moment Manchester United lost at Hull on the opening weekend, just as Ruben Amorim was doomed from the moment cameras picked him up fiddling with magnetic counters on a tactics board in the rain at Grimsby. The message for Mauricio Pochettino is clear: don’t go playing badly on the east coast.

It’s generally acknowledged that Carrick, while he may not have been the ideal manager for United, was a long way down the list of the biggest problems at the club. So what was the point of sacking him? As Pochettino begins his United career at Anfield on Sunday, what realistically can any manager hope to achieve?

articles.title: Erasmus runs risk of breaching World Rugby ban with watchalong
articles.summary: South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus went ahead with an online watchalong during Ireland's victory over his team in the Nations Championship on Saturday.
body: Erasmus is serving a six-match suspension handed down by World Rugby following extraordinary claims, questioning whether "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby after his side's defeat to France in Paris last week.
The 54-year-old was suspended for "public criticism of match officials, undermining the integrity of individuals or the sport, and fuelling online abuse".

After a brief welcome, Erasmus kept himself on mute during both halves of the match, where he could be seen clapping at times, gazing intently at a TV, apparently shouting into what presumably was a phone and thumping his table in frustration when Ireland won 20-17.
But he did come off mute at half-time to outline what he thought would be under discussion in the break. He said: "We've not been playing perfect.

articles.title: Bournemouth make more history with comfortable win against Forest
articles.summary: Bournemouth continued their unstoppable form with a comfortable 2-0 victory against Nottingham Forest and created two bits of history in the process.
body: It was a club-record ninth successive win in all competitions and the first time they have won five in a row in the Premier League. They have kept seven clean sheets in those games as well - only conceding against Ipswich in the league - with 23 goals scored.

A large part of that has been down to the form of Evanilson, and the Brazilian did not disappoint. He struck first with a wonderful effort - set up by the deftest of headers from James Hill - to extend his scoring run to six straight Premier League games.
It was a simple but effective break for Bournemouth's second as Forest failed to follow up a big win against Manchester City before the international break.
Marcus Tavernier sped down the left-hand side, with only Justin Kluivert for support. That was all he needed, though, as his low cross was turned home by the Netherlands international.

body: Unai Emery's side had 72 per cent possession but failed to make their dominance on the ball count with an expected goals value of just 0.98 xG accumulated.

Opportunities to break the deadlock within the tepid performance were limited to half-chances through Emi Buendia's attempted chip in the first half and Leon Goretzka's shot, which was skewed wide from close range.

Captain John McGinn, who was a shock omission from the starting line-up, sparked a degree of urgency with his introduction at the hour mark and orchestrated the only real goalscoring chance for his side.
The midfielder pulled the ball across the face of goal but substitute Brian Madjo, 17, who had replaced Nicolas Jackson moments earlier, was nowhere to be seen to tap it home.

articles.title: 49ers' Nick Bosa criticizes Mexican fans, kicks off internet firestorm
articles.summary: Ahead of the 49ers ' biggest game of the season thus far - a date with the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City - struggling star edge rusher Nick Bosa appears to have made himself public enemy No. 1 with Mexican fans.
body: In a meeting with reporters earlier this week in Colorado Springs, where the 49ers spent preparation time ahead of their travel to Mexico City to help adjust to the high altitude, Bosa issued bizarre comments about Mexican fans that sparked reaction from fans and reporters alike.

"I think we need some like information given to fans so they know when to cheer," Bosa said in regard to Mexican fans. "... They just chant the whole time... no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques."
Bosa would later joke that it would be "great" if they could cheer primarily when the 49ers are on defense.
The clip notably spawned reaction from several reporters, including two reporters from ESPN and 49ers reporter Grant Cohn, who all put Bosa on blast for the "embarrassing" and "super weird" comments.

articles.title: BYU Holds on in 3OT Win Over Kansas
articles.summary: You probably said some choice words, but a Bear Bachmeier two-point conversion completion to JoJo Phillips in triple overtime lifted BYU in a 31-29 win over Kansas Saturday in Lawrence.
body: BYU went into half down 6-3, but two third quarter interceptions from the defense allowed BYU to pull ahead 16-6 going into the fourth quarter. Kansas tied the game, and Matthias Dunn shanked a kick on the last play of regulation.

Kansas has played teams tight this year, but it doesn’t feel good to scrape by a 4-6 team. LJ Martin played most of the game, and while he was bottled up for much of the game, came through in the end and ran for 127 yards. Bear Bachmeier passed for 173 yards and added 59 rushing yards and 2 rushing TDs.
Stats were even across the board, which is not surprising considering the result. Both teams had 2 turnovers and outgained Kansas 381-359.
Next we’ll see how the committee treats BYU after the result. Regardless, BYU’s CFP and Big 12 title game hopes remain alive when BYU hosts Cincinnati next Saturday in the final regular season game.

body: Of course, this isn't a perfect offense, which was evident back in Week 9 when Caleb Williams threw four interceptions, granted, not all were his fault. Still, this elite Bears offense can get better. But how?
